claims.text: Sustained loading causes FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers to progress from homogeneous dislocation slip toward localized deformation twinning and strain-induced short-range ordering.
Constrained nanoscale layer interfaces primarily govern the proposed deformation transition.
Nanoscale interfaces enhance local stress concentrations.
Nanoscale interfaces facilitate activation of subsidiary slip systems.
Interface-mediated activation of slip and twinning balances strength with deformability.
The starting coating contains alternating FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The starting multilayer exhibits lattice distortion and initial short-range chemical order.
Varying layer thickness during controlled-temperature creep testing can expose the role of interfacial spacing.
Interfaces accentuate lattice distortion and modify local short-range order.
Grain or phase boundaries in high-entropy alloys can act as sites for defect nucleation and produce uneven local stresses.
Constrained geometry and compositional gradients create stress concentrations that lower the barrier to twin formation.
Short-range order evolves during sustained loading.
Evolving short-range order impedes dislocation motion.
Sustained loading will increase deformation-twin density relative to the starting baseline.
Sustained loading will produce measurable changes in local ordering near layer interfaces.
A critical interfacial dimension or stress threshold marks the onset of the mechanistic shift.
Baseline multilayers deform predominantly by homogeneous dislocation activity and show minimal twinning or strain-induced ordering.
The hypothesis applies below approximately 100 nm layer thickness and where diffusion-mediated effects are minimal.
TEM, diffraction, and atom-probe measurements can track dislocations, twins, and local ordering during or after creep.
Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in interfacial twinning or short-range-order changes relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as as-deposited and unstrained, yet it is also said to deform predominantly by homogeneous dislocation activity. An unstrained as-deposited state cannot itself have an active deformation mode unless a separate baseline loading protocol is specified.
